headline: A South Dakota Community Comes Together to Free an Owl from Barbed Wire
meta_description: When a great horned owl became tangled in barbed wire near Spearfish, South Dakota, strangers and neighbors united to free it, demonstrating the power of compa…
summary_short: Strangers stopped to help free a great horned owl trapped in barbed wire near Spearfish, South Dakota. A veterinarian examined it, and a wildlife center will release it…
body:
When Sharon Jacobs spotted what looked like a lump of feathers caught in a barbed wire fence near Spearfish, South Dakota, she asked her husband Scott to stop the car. What she found was a living great horned owl—not the dead hawk Scott had initially thought he saw—tangled and injured. What followed was a testament to community: within the hour, a handful of strangers and locals had assembled at the roadside, each contributing exactly what was needed to free the bird without causing further harm. A passing driver named Brandon had gloves when the team needed protection from the owl's talons. He also had wirecutters. The landowner's daughter appeared and connected her father by phone, who immediately authorized cutting the wire. A veterinarian agreed to meet them after hours and carefully removed two steel barbs embedded in the bird's body.

The rescue didn't end at the clinic. Sharon then called every nearby wildlife center to find the best equipped to care for a wounded owl, settling on Black Hills Raptor Center. The center plans to release the owl back to the same area where it was found—and Sharon has promised to be there when it happens. "Everybody's goal was to get this beautiful creature taken care of," she told Cowboy State Daily, reflecting on how quickly people had mobilized to help.

What makes this rescue remarkable isn't just that it succeeded, but how it unfolded. No single person had all the tools or expertise needed. Instead, each person who stopped or answered a call brought one piece of the puzzle. The veterinarian confirmed the owl would fly again. Brandon had the gloves and cutters. The landowner gave permission. Sharon provided the determination to see it through. In a moment when it would have been easy to drive past, an entire community chose to stop and care.
quick_facts: Great horned owl trapped in barbed wire near Spearfish, South Dakota
Strangers and neighbors united to free the bird within hours
Veterinarian removed two steel barbs; owl will recover and fly again
Black Hills Raptor Center will release owl back to the wild
